chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Hafsh al-Marwazi, from the Faqih (peace be upon him), who said:

"When a man performs Hajj al-Tamattu', enters Mecca, performs Tawaf around the House, prays two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim (peace be upon him), performs Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and shortens his prayer, then everything becomes permissible for him except women, because for the解除 of women, there is a Tawaf and a prayer."

This is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because in the report it is not stated whether the Tawaf and Sa'i after which one may have intercourse (before the Tawaf of women) are for the Umrah or for the Hajj. If the report does not specify this, we interpret it as referring to one who performs Tawaf and Sa'i for Hajj, for he is not permitted to have intercourse with women. This interpretation is preferable because the statement of the Faqih (peace be upon him) in the report is explanatory: 'because for the解除 of women, there is a Tawaf and a prayer.' This indicates that the Umrah performed for Tamattu' to Hajj does not require the Tawaf of women; rather, the Tawaf of women is required in the Umrah al-Mufradah or in Hajj.

And that which indicates this is what was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: Abu al-Qasim Mukhallad ibn Musa al-Razi wrote to the Man (peace be upon him) asking him about the Umrah al-Mufradah, is there upon its owner the Tawaf of women? And about the Umrah that one performs for Tamattu' to Hajj? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'As for the Umrah al-Mufradah, upon its owner is the Tawaf of women. And as for the one that is performed for Tamattu' to Hajj, upon its owner is not the Tawaf of women.'

And it is not appropriate for one performing Umrah al-Tamattu' to leave Mecca before he has completed all its rituals, except for necessity. If he is compelled to leave, he leaves to a place where Hajj is not missed, and he exits in Hajj state. If he can return to Mecca, he does so; otherwise, he proceeds to Arafat. If he leaves without Ihram and then returns, if his return is in the same month he left in, it does not harm him to enter Mecca without Ihram. And if he enters in a different month than the one he left in, he enters it in Ihram for Umrah al-Tamattu', and his final Umrah is that which he performs for Tamattu' to Hajj. He narrated that.

key_terms.السَّعْيُ: Sa'i: The ritual walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah.
key_terms.حَجُّ التَّمَتُّعِ: Hajj al-Tamattu': A type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj, with a解除 period in between.
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa': The specific Tawaf performed after the initial rituals to解除 the prohibition of sexual intercourse for the pilgrim.
key_terms.عُمْرَةُ الْمُفْتَرَدَةُ: Umrah al-Mufradah: An independent Umrah, distinct from the Umrah of Tamattu'.
key_terms.مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Maqam Ibrahim: The station of Abraham, behind which the two rak'ahs of prayer are performed after Tawaf.

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a man performing Hajj al-Tamattu' to be permitted to have intercourse with his wife, and what is the role of Tawaf al-Nisa?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this hadith to resolve the juristic debate regarding whether the initial rites of Umrah al-Tamattu' suffice for marital intimacy or if a separate Tawaf al-Nisa' is required. By citing the correspondence of Abu al-Qasim al-Razi with the Imam, the text clarifies that while Umrah al-Mufradah mandates Tawaf al-Nisa', the Umrah of Tamattu' does not, thereby permitting intimacy after the first Tawaf and Sa'i. This distinction underscores the Shia view that the 'Tamattu'' Umrah is a preparatory act rather than a complete independent pilgrimage.
